title: This fish marries by melting together
script: This fish marries by melting together. In some deep sea anglerfish, the tiny male bites a female and never lets go. Their skin and blood vessels fuse, and he slowly becomes part of her body. She carries him for life.
description: The strangest marriage in the ocean.

title: This fish has a see-through head
script: This fish has a see-through head. The barreleye lives hundreds of meters down, and its bright green eyes sit inside a clear dome of fluid. They can rotate to look straight up. Those two dots on its face? Just nostrils.
description: Meet the fish you can look straight into.

title: It skipped dinner for five years
script: This creature skipped dinner for five years. A giant isopod at an aquarium in Japan refused food from 2009 until it died in 2014. These deep sea relatives of pill bugs can grow over 40 centimeters long. Imagine one in your garden.
description: The deep sea scavenger that barely needs to eat.

title: This animal has eyes like dinner plates
script: This animal has eyes like dinner plates. The colossal squid has the largest eyes of any known animal, about 27 centimeters across. They likely help it spot hunting sperm whales in the dark. Yours are about 2.4 centimeters.
description: The biggest eyes on the planet belong to a squid.

title: Most deep sea animals make their own light
script: Most deep sea animals glow. A 2017 study off California found 76 percent of animals filmed down to 3,900 meters make their own light. They use it to hunt, hide and find mates. The darkest place on Earth is full of light.
description: Why the deep ocean is not as dark as you think.
